deals.proximityHighways: Frontage on S. College Street (US-127), the principal north-south route through Harrodsburg, roughly 30 miles southwest of Lexington. The OM does not print a traffic count.
deals.retailCotenants: Kroger is the dominant grocer in the trade area with Walmart the only other major grocery operator in the market. Nearby demand generators include downtown Harrodsburg, Mercer County Senior High School, The Willows at Harrodsburg senior living community, Bright Leaf Golf Resort and three manufacturing facilities. The 958-acre Bluegrass Innovation Gateway industrial development is planned for the area.

tenants.assumptionNote: 18 years of tenure. No sales disclosed.

tenants.name: Smoke World
tenants.rentSchedule: Flat $8.43/SF ($15,173) in CY2027. The January 2032 expiry ASSUMES the tenant exercises its contractual option — see the assumption note.
tenants.renewalOptions: Contractual option that would run the term to January 2032, with OPTION NOTICE DUE 8/1/2026. CBRE's analysis assumes the option is exercised.
tenants.assumptionNote: READ THE OM FOOTNOTE ON THIS ONE. Per footnote [3], the lease actually EXPIRES 1/31/2027 with option notice due 8/1/2026, and OWNERSHIP BELIEVES THE TENANT MAY MISS THE NOTICE DATE — but plans to negotiate a higher-rent renewal afterward. CBRE's model nonetheless assumes the tenant executes its contractual option, which is what produces the January 2032 expiry shown here and keeps 1,800 SF in the occupied column at $8.43/SF. Confirm the current status of the notice before crediting either the term or the rent. At $8.43/SF this is materially below the $12.00/SF shop market rent, so a missed option is arguably an opportunity rather than a loss — but it is a change in occupancy either way. Tobacco/vape is also a regulatory- and headline-risk use.

tenants.name: Kroger
tenants.rentSchedule: Flat $7.05/SF ($254,914) in CY2027 through the September 2028 current-term expiry. The OM does not print the option rents.
tenants.renewalOptions: THREE remaining five-year options per the p.3 highlights, which would carry the term to roughly September 2043. Kroger exercised its most recent option in 2023 WITHOUT landlord concessions. The OM does not print the option rents — get them from the lease.
tenants.creditRating: Investment grade (The Kroger Co. — BBB category)
tenants.assumptionNote: THE DEAL. 60% of GLA, 51% of base rent, 52.2% of total revenue, and an exceptional store: $858 PSF of 2025 sales (approximately $31.0M) at a 1.10% health ratio (OM-stated) — one of the strongest grocery occupancy costs you will see, and up 13% since 2022. In place since October 1987 (nearly 40 years) and exercised its most recent option in 2023 with no landlord concessions, which is the clearest possible signal of commitment. Three five-year options remain. It also pays a token $934 of percentage rent, meaning sales are just over the breakpoint. At $7.05/SF the rent is far below any market measure but is effectively locked by the option chain to ~2043 — this is SECURE, extremely sticky income, not capturable mark-to-market. CBRE excludes Kroger from the general vacancy-loss factor.

tenants.name: Arby's
tenants.rentSchedule: Flat $34.69/SF ($79,440) in CY2027 through the June 2028 expiry.
tenants.parentCompany: Inspire Brands (Arby's — franchised location; franchisee not disclosed)
tenants.assumptionNote: Pad-site QSR and the second-largest rent at the center, $79,440 at $34.69/SF — 16% of base rent on 3.8% of GLA. In place since June 1988 (38 years) with $472 PSF of sales at a 7.93% health ratio (OM-stated), which is workable for a QSR but not cheap. EXPIRES JUNE 2028 with no disclosed option, and CBRE's model assumes a holdover at current terms. Because the rent is so far above the rest of the center, losing this pad would hurt disproportionately — and $34.69/SF is well above CBRE's own $35.00/SF pad market rent only in the sense that it is already at market, so there is no renewal upside here. Confirm the franchisee and any guaranty.

keyAssumptions: ROSTER BASIS: CBRE's IN-PLACE PRO-FORMA for calendar year 2027 (page 9), which is what the $455,218 in-place NOI, the $140,226 recovery line, the $12,789 percentage rent and the $654,519 effective gross revenue all tie to. This OM prints FULL lease dates (MM/DD/YY) on the pro-forma, so no date convention was needed.

Four-way tie-out against the OM's printed totals: (a) 56,448 SF occupied + 3,600 SF vacant = 60,048 SF GLA; (b) 56,448 / 60,048 = 94.0% occupancy; (c) base rents sum to $501,504 = the printed Total Tenant Revenue Occupied; (d) $654,519 EGR - $199,301 OpEx = $455,218 NOI. Tenant recoveries sum to $140,227 vs the $140,226 printed (rounding), and percentage rent sums to $12,789 exactly.

WALT of 2.07 years is the OM-stated figure and reproduces exactly when computed SF-weighted from the roster's expiries as of 01/01/2027 (the analysis commencement date) — an independent confirmation the roster is complete. Note this is a CURRENT-TERM WALT: Kroger's three remaining five-year options would extend the effective term to roughly 2043 and are not in the 2.07.

SMOKE WORLD'S TERM IS AN ASSUMPTION, NOT A FACT. Footnote [3] states the lease expires 1/31/2027 with option notice due 8/1/2026, that ownership believes the tenant MAY MISS the notice date, and that ownership plans to negotiate a higher-rent renewal afterward — yet CBRE models the option as exercised, producing the 1/31/2032 expiry shown on the roster. Confirm the notice status; the outcome changes both occupancy and the rent on 1,800 SF.

FEEDERS PET SUPPLY IS A GROSS LEASE and the only one at the center — zero expense reimbursement is modeled on its 5,400 SF (9% of GLA), so ownership carries CAM, taxes and insurance there. It also pays $11,855 of percentage rent, which is what makes its total occupancy cost a healthy 4.72%.
NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $455,218 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED. The $65,252 CY2027 tax line is the 2026 budget grown forward; the OM states expressly that reassessment is the investor's responsibility. Mercer County, KY assesses at fair cash value, so a sale will very likely reset the assessment to the purchase price — the modeled tax line is 14% of NOI.

AN UNUSUALLY LARGE CAPITAL AMORTIZATION RECOVERY sits below the NOI line: $40,961 in CY2027, declining to zero by CY2035. That is tenant reimbursement of amortized deferred capital projects, which CBRE models below the line per its standard note — it is NOT in the $455,218 NOI, but it IS real cash in the early years. Do not double-count it, and understand it burns off.

The OM does not print a traffic count for US-127 / S. College Street, a year built, a renovation year, individual rent steps, or any co-tenancy, exclusive or kickout clause. All left null rather than estimated.

RECENT CAPITAL: the OM states ownership has completed repaving of the parking lots, facade updates and roof maintenance, positioning the asset with minimal near-term capital needs. No scope, cost or dates are given — ask for the capital ledger and a roof report rather than taking the claim at face value.

redFlags.description: 79% OF GLA ROLLS IN 2028. Kroger's current term ends September 2028 (36,158 SF), Arby's June 2028 (2,290 SF), Emily Nails July 2028 and Lexington Urgent Care May 2028 — CBRE's own schedule shows 42,048 SF expiring in 2028 and 79.02% cumulative. Kroger's three remaining five-year options make its renewal highly likely (it exercised in 2023 with no concessions and runs a $858 PSF store), but the concentration is extreme and everything about the deal turns on that option being exercised again.

Feeders Pet Supply expires 28 February 2027, two months into the analysis period, on 9% of GLA — and it is a GROSS lease with no expense recovery. CBRE's in-place NOI simply assumes a holdover at current terms, carrying no downtime or re-leasing cost.

Smoke World's roster term is modeled, not contractual. The OM itself says the lease expires 1/31/2027, that option notice was due 8/1/2026, and that OWNERSHIP BELIEVES THE TENANT MAY MISS IT. CBRE nonetheless assumes the option is exercised. That is 1,800 SF and $15,173 of rent whose status the seller is openly uncertain about.

Arby's is 16% of base rent on 3.8% of GLA at $34.69/SF, expires June 2028 with no disclosed option, and already sits at CBRE's modeled pad market rent — so there is no renewal upside, only renewal risk. Its 7.93% occupancy cost is fine but not comfortable.

The trade area is small and slow: 3-mile population of 10,510 growing 0.19% annually, 3-mile average household income of $68,376 and median of $56,038, with a 5-year AHHI growth rate of only 6.84% — the weakest income growth in this portfolio group. Total 3-mile households are 4,430. This argues for cap-rate cushion, not aggressive rent growth, and it caps what shop space can realistically be pushed to.

Aside from Kroger, sales are disclosed for only two tenants (Feeders Pet Supply and Arby's). Nothing is known about the health of Cricket Wireless, Wah Mei Chinese, Emily Nails, Smoke World, Lexington Urgent Care or The UPS Store.
Taxes are NOT reassessed in the pro-forma. The $65,252 modeled tax line is 14% of NOI and a Kentucky sale typically triggers reassessment to the transaction price.
The $40,961 of CY2027 capital-amortization recovery below the NOI line burns off entirely by 2035. It is real cash today but it is not durable income, and it should not be capitalized.

upsideItems.detail: Lease up the 3,600 SF vacancy — CBRE models 12-month absorption from 1/1/2027 (first absorption 1/1/2028) at $10.00-$12.00/SF small-shop market rent, NNN + 15% admin. The OM notes the space may be DIVISIBLE into smaller suites, which typically raises the achievable PSF materially on a 3,600 SF box — at the cost of higher TI and demising work.

upsideItems.item: Shop mark-to-market against a fresh $14.00/SF UPS lease
upsideItems.detail: Genuine shop mark-to-market: Wah Mei Chinese at $8.14/SF, Smoke World at $8.43/SF and Cricket Wireless at $10.75/SF all sit well below the $14.00/SF The UPS Store signed in April 2026 on a fresh 10-year lease. That UPS Store deal is the single best read on real shop market rent at this center, and it is roughly 40-70% above three in-place shop rents. In-place $8.88/SF versus CBRE's $10.60/SF 2027 market rent is the aggregate gap.

upsideItems.item: Kroger's option chain secures income to ~2043
upsideItems.detail: Kroger's option chain is the income anchor: three remaining five-year options would carry the term to roughly 2043, and the tenant exercised in 2023 with no landlord concessions on the back of $858 PSF sales and a 1.10% occupancy cost. This is exceptionally durable, sticky income — the $7.05/SF is not capturable upside, but its security is what makes the rest of the business plan financeable.

upsideItems.item: Kroger percentage rent is already live and growing
upsideItems.detail: Kroger already pays percentage rent ($934 in CY2027), meaning sales have crossed the breakpoint. With sales up 13% since 2022 and modeled to keep growing, the percentage-rent line grows from $12,789 in CY2027 to $135,543 by CY2037 in CBRE's projection — a meaningful and often overlooked component of the 4.93% NOI CAGR.

upsideItems.item: Only two grocers serve the market
upsideItems.detail: Limited grocery competition: Walmart is the only other major grocer in the market, and Kroger is the dominant destination in the trade area.

Recent capital reduces near-term spend: ownership reports repaved parking lots, updated facades and maintained roofs. Verify with a capital ledger and roof report, but if it holds, going-in capex should be light.

upsideItems.item: Bluegrass Innovation Gateway could reset the trade area
upsideItems.detail: The planned 958-acre Bluegrass Innovation Gateway industrial development could materially reset a small trade area's job base and household income. It is planned, not built — treat as optionality, not underwriting.

deals.notes: Harrodsburg Marketplace is a 60,048 SF Kroger-anchored neighborhood center on S. College Street (US-127) in Harrodsburg, Kentucky, roughly 30 miles southwest of Lexington, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. The story is the anchor: Kroger has operated here since October 1987, occupies 60% of the GLA at $7.05/SF, does $858 PSF of 2025 sales (about $31.0 million, up 13% since 2022) at a 1.10% health ratio, exercised its most recent option in 2023 without landlord concessions, and holds three more five-year options that would carry the term to roughly 2043. That is as strong a grocery credit position as this portfolio offers, and it produces 52% of the center's revenue. In-place CY2027 NOI is $455,218 on $654,519 of effective gross revenue against $199,301 of operating expenses, at an $8.88/SF weighted-average base rent versus CBRE's $10.60/SF modeled market rent. Below the anchor the picture is thinner. WALT is only 2.07 years on current terms, 79% of GLA is scheduled to roll in 2028, and the near-term roll starts almost immediately: Feeders Pet Supply, a gross lease with no expense recovery on 9% of the GLA, expires in February 2027, and Smoke World's roster term is a modeled option exercise that the OM itself says ownership expects the tenant may miss. Arby's, at 16% of base rent on a 3.8%-of-GLA pad, expires June 2028 already at market rent. The value-add case is the single 3,600 SF vacancy plus genuine mark-to-market on Wah Mei Chinese at $8.14/SF and Cricket Wireless at $10.75/SF against a $14.00/SF UPS Store lease signed in April 2026 — the best available read on real shop market rent here. The constraint is the trade area: 10,510 people within three miles, $68,376 average household income and the slowest income growth in this group, which limits how far shop rents can be pushed and argues for cap-rate cushion behind an otherwise excellent grocery box.
